I've been reading some of Herman Melville's short stories and in "The Piazza" came across this sentence that just instantly imbedded itself in my heart. I had to stop and reread it several times because it had a true frisson effect on me.

"For the way now lay where path was none, and none might go but by himself, and only go by daring."

I'd love to hear sentences that have had that kind of effect on you!
Have you ever read a sentence in a book that made you stop in your tracks?

Don't remember the exact sentance, but it was in a book called Pine Island Paradox. The basic idea was that love is taking someone's hand, pointing it at something new, and saying "look!"--basically learning and appreciating together. I don't think it was a very popular book, but that sentence changed my entire view of relationships and I think about it frequently for years now.

I'll have to check out that book. I know it's kind of cheesy but it's one of the things I love most about books, they showcase the power of words: someone you'll most likely never meet strings a few words together and they can change your perspective about life. It's just amazing to me!

The Utterly Perfect Murder by Ray Bradbury.

"At some secret blood level, I had always known I would not use the weapon. I had

brought it with me, yes, but Time had gotten here before me, and age, and smaller, more terrible deaths....

Bang.

Six shots through the heart."
How fantastic is Bradbury; I've never read The Utterly Perfect Murder but it's definitely going on my to-read list now.
It is really a short story rather then a book, but never the less breath taking.
I hope one day you get the pleasure of it!

Book 4 of Paradise Lost The devil is lamenting on his lost glory and realizes this in a moment of rare insight.

...

From me, whom he created what I was

In that bright eminence, and with his good

Upbraided none; nor was his service hard.

What could be less than to afford him praise,

The easiest recompense, and pay him thanks,

How due, yet all his good proved ill in me,

And wrought but malice ...

The 'how due' part really took my breath away; it was the most unexpected thing I would ever imagine the devil to say.

That is beautiful. I haven't read many classics like Paradise Lost, I find it hard to get past the language barrier and really into the story but I'm hoping it's one of those things that gets easier the more I practice with it.
Try Paradiselost.org They give the modern equivallent along side the original in PLAIN ENGLISH mode.
